content: agent2: adding process_priority param to click.edit() (termui.py) and Editor class (_termui_impl.py: __init__, edit_files/edit via Popen preexec/creationflags). Will touch only those two files. What is your feature / which lines?

agent2 plan to avoid overlap. You own edit_file->edit_files and the Popen call. I will NOT touch the body of edit_file(s). Request: in your subprocess.Popen(...) call please add the kwarg **self._priority_popen_kwargs() (I define that method on Editor, placed right after get_editor(), returns {} when no priority/unsupported; on Unix it gives preexec_fn, on Windows creationflags). My edits: (1) Editor.__init__ in _termui_impl.py: add 'process_priority: str | None = None' as LAST param + self.process_priority attr, plus the new method after get_editor; (2) termui.py edit(): append 'process_priority: str | None = None,' as the LAST param (after your new/changed params, after filename), a ':param process_priority:' docstring entry at the end of the params, and 'process_priority=process_priority' in the Editor(...) construction. If you add overloads, please include process_priority: str | None = None as the last arg in each. Reply with your final Popen form + signature if different.

Please write it as: c = subprocess.Popen(<your cmd line>, env=environ, shell=True, **self._priority_popen_kwargs(),) vertical, i.e. one extra line '**self._priority_popen_kwargs(),' after 'shell=True,'. The method exists in my patch (defined between Editor.__init__ and get_editor, so not adjacent to your edit_file hunk). Please confirm the splat line is in your patch.

agent2: agreed on ownership. You own the edit() signature (with "process_priority: str | None = None," last, in both overloads) and the docstring; I own only the Editor(...) construction in the body (vertical form, ending process_priority=process_priority,) and _termui_impl.py outside edit_files/Popen/the self.edit_files((name,)) call; _priority_popen_kwargs sits between __init__ and get_editor. Doc text to paste verbatim at the end of the params (after your :param filename: text), continuation lines aligned under the text:
    :param process_priority: the CPU priority to start the editor process
                             with: ``'low'``, ``'below_normal'``,
                             ``'normal'``, ``'above_normal'`` or
                             ``'high'``.  By default, or for any other
                             value, the editor starts with the priority
                             it would otherwise get.  Raising the
                             priority usually needs privileges, and when
                             the priority cannot be set the editor
                             starts anyway, with the default one.
Then, after your versionchanged block at the end of the docstring:
    .. versionadded:: 8.2.0
        The ``process_priority`` parameter.
(i.e. write the quote marks around the five values as double backticks around single-quoted words, e.g. ``low`` in single quotes.) Note my Editor(...) call passes process_priority=process_priority, so the name must be the signature parameter.
